title: Sign commits
loadError: The signing settings could not be loaded
blocked: Choose an SSH key first – without it, every commit fails.
repoIntro: Applies only to this repository (.git/config) and takes precedence over the global setting.
globalIntro: Applies to all repositories that don't set their own (global Git configuration). Every commit from this app is signed – just like in the terminal.
sameAsGlobal: Currently the same as the global setting applies here.

format.title: Format
format.description: What signs the commits (gpg.format). Changing the format means choosing the key again.

sshKey.title: SSH key
sshKey.none: No SSH key added yet. Create one under “SSH keys” on the left or add an existing one – then it can be chosen here.
sshKey.description: The public key whose private counterpart signs the commits (user.signingKey). You can choose from the keys under “SSH keys”.

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.description: Identifier of the certificate for gpgsm (user.signingKey). Empty: gpgsm uses the certificate for your email address.

keyId.title: Key ID
keyId.description: ID or fingerprint of your GPG key (user.signingKey), e.g. from “gpg --list-secret-keys”. Empty: GPG uses the key for your email address.

enable.title: Sign commits
enable.ssh: Every new commit gets an SSH signature (commit.gpgSign). Git only shows it as “valid” once gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile knows your key – otherwise the commit shows “cannot be verified”.
enable.other: Every new commit is signed (commit.gpgSign). If the program cannot ask for the passphrase, the commit fails with Git's message.

program.title: Program
program.description: Read-only: the program Git starts for signing ({{config}}). For now it can only be changed with git config.

global.summaryNoKey: Global setting: {{state}}, {{format}}, without a fixed key.
